title: bl_cli docs say each module registers its own commands, while backlog.py registers bl_view, bl_land, bl_ci, bl_plan and bl_check's
goal: Either every bl_ module that owns a command registers its parser and handler with bl_cli itself (importing the module registers it, in usage order), or the bl_cli.py docstring, kb/_self/tools.md (bl_cli row) and kb/_self/code.md say backlog.py registers them; the sprint clause 'each registers its own parsers' (SP-tpulmoxh) is met or its docs stop claiming it. Found by the SP-tpulmoxh review.

gates.question: Which way closes the gap between the docs and the code on who registers each bl_ module's commands?
options: each bl_ module that owns a command registers it itself, and backlog.py imports the modules in usage order, as bl_cost and bl_procs do (meets the sprint's 'each registers its own parsers')
backlog.py keeps registering them, and the bl_cli.py docstring, tools.md's bl_cli row and code.md say so
gates.recommendation: each bl_ module that owns a command registers it itself, and backlog.py imports the modules in usage order, as bl_cost and bl_procs do (meets the sprint's 'each registers its own parsers')
gates.answer: each bl_ module that owns a command registers it itself, and backlog.py imports the modules in usage order, as bl_cost and bl_procs do (meets the sprint's 'each registers its own parsers')
